cases.name: Nomad Bridge
cases.audit_note: Quantstamp audited the Nomad stack; report item QSP-19 flagged that a zero trusted root should be rejected, but a zero _committedRoot was still used in the Replica initialize() and accepted as valid.
cases.bug: The freshly initialized Ethereum Replica was deployed with _committedRoot set to 0x00, which the routine root-confirmation path accepts as a proven root, letting anyone forge messages that withdraw funds from the bridge.
cases.gaps: Nomad's Replica is a standalone contract, not a proxy, so proxy_address is null and there is no previous implementation; 'previous_address' null reflects the architecture, not missing data. Loss figure is the rekt.news estimate.

cases.name: Ronin Network (MainchainGatewayV3)
cases.audit_note: rekt.news tags the incident Unaudited; the new MainchainGatewayV3 implementation (deployed 6 days before the upgrade) was not audited.
cases.bug: The new implementation was initialized with initializeV4() instead of first running initializeV3(), leaving _totalOperatorWeight at zero and thereby disabling the minimum-vote-weight check, so a single compromised/attacker operator address could alone pass unlock (withdrawal) votes.
cases.gaps: The previous (V2) implementation address was not stated in any opened source, so previous_address is null. Attack was executed by MEV bot 0x4Ab12E7CE31857Ee022f273e8580F73335a73c0B in block 20468679; rekt leaderboard lists 08/07 but on-chain timestamps are 2024-08-06 08:48:47 UTC (upgrade) and 09:37:23 UTC (exploit), so both events are Aug 6 UTC.

cases.name: LI.FI (GasZipFacet)
cases.audit_note: rekt.news audit field shows n/a for this incident; no audit of the new facet was referenced.
cases.bug: The newly added GasZipFacet allowed arbitrary calldata to be injected into its swap validation, so anyone could craft a swap call that drained user-approved tokens from the LiFi diamond.
cases.gaps: exploit_tx is null: the full hash of the first attack transaction was not present in any opened source; exploit date 2024-07-16 comes from the rekt article and a CertiK tweet (tweet-ID timestamp 2024-07-16 ~12:29 UTC). The facet was created via factory 0x93FEC2C00BfE902F733B57c5a6CeeD7CD1384AE1; the vulnerable diamond is 0x1231deb6f5749ef6ce6943a275a1d3e7486f4eae, so proxy_address is null because the diamond is not an upgradeable proxy in the classic sense.

cases.name: Socket (WrappedTokenSwapper route)
cases.audit_note: Socket had PeckShield and Consensys Diligence audits, but the newly registered WrappedTokenSwapper route was outside the audited scope.
cases.bug: The unvalidated swap logic in the newly added WrappedTokenSwapper implementation let an attacker pass a malicious swap target, causing the SocketGateway to transfer tokens on the attacker's terms.
cases.gaps: Route is a standalone implementation registered on SocketGateway 0x3a23f943181408eac424116af7b7790c94cb97a5 (registration tx 0x1df44e22...), so proxy_address and previous_address are null. Creation timestamp 2024-01-13 05:16:59 UTC verified on-chain; creator 0x8BE6C8b2cA6f39fd70C9DdF35B4c34301AE10c0F.

cases.name: SushiSwap (RouteProcessor2)
cases.audit_note: rekt.news tags the incident Unaudited; no audit of RouteProcessor2 was referenced.
cases.bug: The uniswapV3SwapCallback in RouteProcessor2 did not verify that the calling pool was legitimately deployed by the canonical Uniswap V3 factory, letting the attacker spoof a pool and steal approved tokens during swaps.
cases.gaps: Standalone router contract (not a proxy), so proxy_address and previous_address are null. live timestamp 2023-04-05 06:46:59 UTC and exploit timestamp 2023-04-09 02:35:23 UTC verified on-chain.

cases.name: Unizen
cases.audit_note: Protocol had Halborn and Verichains audits from 2022, but the March 2024 upgrade itself was not audited (rekt.news lists Halborn, Verichains).
cases.bug: The freshly upgraded contract performed an external call without verifying its destination, letting the attacker redirect the swap/transfer flow and drain funds held by the proxy.
cases.gaps: previous_address null (prior implementation not identified in opened sources). The proxy is TransparentUpgradeableProxy 0xd3f64BAa... (current post-fix implementation 0x97B8210dFe6e970190c7496511F7318C91756a8b per blockscout); the linkage between the created implementation 0xA051Fc7D... and the proxy at upgrade time is presumed from the upgrade tx but was not directly confirmed. Upgrade timestamp 2024-03-08 12:38:23 UTC, exploit 20:13:35 UTC; a second attack tx 0x30fef86a72ea7e1109ffeae572439995c78561ffeb968dcbd61c609efc60fdd9. Loss is rekt's $2.1M (leaderboard's $21M appears to be a factor-of-10 error).

cases.name: Sonne Finance (soVELO market)
cases.audit_note: yAudit's 2023 audit had explicitly flagged this Hundred-Finance-style donation attack vector forVELO-collateral markets; the vulnerability went live anyway when the new market was configured.
cases.bug: When the newly deployed VELO market's collateral factor was set to 35% by governance, the interest-rate model allowed a self-transfer/donation attack: an attacker could mint, donate soVELO to inflate exchange rate accounting, borrow against it, and drain the market of liquidity.
cases.gaps: soVELO is an immutable CErc20 contract (not a proxy), so proxy_address and previous_address are null. Creation timestamp 2024-05-10 13:40:13 UTC verified on-chain (deployer 0xFb59Ce8986943163F14C590755b29dB2998F2322, 'Sonne VelodromeV2'); exploit tx timestamp 2024-05-14 22:18:15 UTC. Attacker 0xae4A7cDe7C99fb98B0D5fA414aa40F0300531F43 used attack contract 0x02FA2625825917E9b1F8346a465dE1bBC150C5B9. rekt leaderboard dates it 05/15; on-chain date is May 14 UTC.

cases.name: Bedrock (uniBTC Vault)
cases.audit_note: The upgraded SigmaSupplier implementation was not audited (rekt.news audit field N/A for the incident).
cases.bug: In the new SigmaSupplier implementation NATIVE_BTC was never registered in the token mapping, so totalSupply read as zero, which bypassed the mint-cap check and let the attacker mint 30.8 uniBTC against only 30.8 ETH of real collateral.
cases.gaps: previous_address null and the proxy-upgrade transaction hash unconfirmed: the implementation creation tx (2024-09-25 03:33:11 UTC) was verified on-chain, but the tx that actually pointed the proxy (in place since 2024-04-13) at the new implementation was not found in opened sources. Exploiter per rekt: 0x2bFB373017349820dda2Da8230E6b66739BE9F96; exploit tx timestamp 2024-09-26 18:28:23 UTC.

cases.name: Level Finance (claimMultiple)
cases.audit_note: Quantstamp and Obelisk had audited Level Finance; Quantstamp's post-mortem states the vulnerability was introduced in the upgrade after the audits.
cases.bug: The upgraded LiquidityPool claimMultiple() implementation failed to mark claimed epochs as spent, allowing the same liquidity-pool tokens to be repeatedly claimed against across epochs and drained of rewards.
cases.gaps: BSC explorer (bscscan) was unreachable in this environment, so the Apr-18-2023 upgrade and May-1-2023 exploit tx hashes/timestamps are taken from the rekt article and Quantstamp's public statement rather than verified on-chain; previous_address (implementation before the upgrade) was not identified.

cases.name: Radiant Capital (attacker-upgraded lending pools)
cases.audit_note: The attacker-deployed implementation was by definition not audited; the compromise vector was a 3-of-11 Safe multisig signing transaction.
cases.bug: After the multisig was compromised, the attacker upgraded the lending pool proxies to a malicious implementation containing a backdoor that transferred the pools' funds to the attacker.
cases.gaps: live_date/live_tx null: rekt says the malicious implementation was 'deployed 14 days ago' (about Oct 2, 2024) but the actual upgrade-go-live transaction could not be confirmed, so days_between is null. Malicious impl copies: Base 0x57ba8957... (ARB), plus ETH 0x3C2Bc83Dcd293Cc8a23526A37aaeEdD83eBd62de and BSC 0xd50Cf00b6e600Dd036Ba8eF475677d816d6c4281; pool proxies: ARB 0xF4B1486DD74D07706052A33d31d7c0AAFD0659E1, BSC 0xd50Cf00b6e600Dd036Ba8eF475677d816d6c4281, ETH 0xA950974f64aA33f27F6C5e017eEE93BF7588ED07, Base 0x30798cFe2CCa822321ceed7e6085e633aAbC492F. BSC exploit tx 0xd97b93f633aee356d992b49193e60a571b8c466bf46aaf072368f975dc11841c; a failed attempt on ARB occurred 6 days prior (0xab34055320676b35d4c6c5936dabc4101b45eda0d66b94ee02f10a96e8a1dd45). Arbitrum/BSC explorers were bot-blocked in this environment, so hashes come from the rekt article without on-chain timestamp confirmation; previous_address null (pre-attack implementation not identified).

cases.name: Conic Finance (CurveLPOracleV2 reentrancy)
cases.audit_note: PeckShield had audited Conic; PeckShield's own analysis noted the newly introduced CurveLPOracleV2 was not part of the audit scope.
cases.bug: The newly introduced CurveLPOracleV2 was vulnerable to a read-only reentrancy attack during uniswap/curve price reads, letting the attacker manipulate LP pricing and drain the UniversalERC20/ETH pools.
cases.gaps: vulnerable_address, live_date, live_tx and days_between null: the exact address of CurveLPOracleV2 and its deployment/go-live transaction were not stated in any opened source (only PeckShield's quote within the rekt article names the contract). Attacker contract 0x743599BA5CfA3cE8c59691aF5ef279AaaFA2E4EB. Loss $4.2M total ($3.3M + $934k across two pools); exploit timestamp 2023-07-21 10:35:11 UTC verified on-chain.

cases.name: Platypus Finance (USP)
cases.audit_note: rekt.news tags the incident Unaudited; the new USP component was not audited at launch.
cases.bug: The emergencyWithdraw/liquidation path's solvency check did not account for borrowed USP in the pool's liabilities, so the attacker could open a USP position, borrow against it, then liquidate themselves profitably, draining pooled assets.
cases.gaps: vulnerable_address and previous_address null: no opened source names the specific vulnerable pool contract address. live_tx null: the USP contract's deployment transaction was not identified; live_date 2023-02-06 comes from Platypus' own Medium recap, and rekt states the exploit occurred 'just 10 days after launch'. Snowtrace/AVAX explorers were unavailable, so the exploit tx hash comes from the rekt article without on-chain timestamp confirmation; tweet-ID timestamps (zachxbt 2023-02-16 ~21:38 UTC, Platypus announcement 2023-02-17 ~01:42 UTC) place the exploit on Feb 16 UTC, while the rekt leaderboard lists 02/17 - discrepancy noted. Attack contract 0x67afdd6489d40a01dae65f709367e1b1d18a5322.

cases.name: Pike Finance
cases.audit_note: No public audit found for Pike Finance at the time of the incident (rekt.news tag: unaudited).
cases.bug: A late-April pause upgrade shifted the storage layout so the initialized flag resolved to false, making the contracts appear uninitialized; the attacker re-initialized them with their own parameters and then used upgradeToAndCall to install a malicious implementation and drain cross-chain funds.
cases.gaps: live_date/live_tx null: the pause-upgrade transaction happened between Apr 26 and Apr 30, 2024 but its exact date/hash was not confirmed in opened sources (an Apr-26-2024 pause tx 0x979ad9b7f5331ea8034305a83b5cd50aea88adec395fff8298dd90eb1b87667f on the Arbitrum target 0x7856493B59cdb1685757A6DcCe12425F6a6666a0 was identified), so days_between is null. Proxy ERC1967 0xFC7599cf... created via 0x0fcc85422e9726a5d8b2ce00291051df0167089e0d1a5e66bfac908c0769e05d by deployer 0xb1eA97c9F68978905fB1Bf5089E71A073bC4f5C8; malicious implementation 0x1da4Bc596BFb1087f2F7999b0340Fcba03C47fbD is the proxy's current implementation per blockscout. Exploit timestamp 2024-04-30 22:19:11 UTC verified on-chain; attacker 0x19066f7431df29a0910d287c8822936bb7d89e23. previous_address (implementation before the pause upgrade) not identified.

dropped.name: Abracadabra Money (MIM)
dropped.reason: Rounding bug resided in legacy CauldronV4 code live since 2021; no recent proxy upgrade or new contract preceded the 2024 exploit.

dropped.name: Seneca
dropped.reason: The vulnerable borrow function had been flawed since the protocol's launch; no recent go-live.

dropped.name: zkLend
dropped.reason: Exploit occurred on Starknet (StarkEx/Cairo), not EVM; out of scope.

dropped.name: KiloEx
dropped.reason: Oracle price-feed address could be set by anyone due to access-control flaw; not a code change that went live shortly before the exploit.

dropped.name: Zunami Protocol
dropped.reason: No confirmed go-live date for the vulnerable change could be established from opened sources.

dropped.name: Hundred Finance
dropped.reason: Donation attack on an empty hWBTC market; the market/bug was not a recent go-live (2023 exploit, vector flagged earlier).

dropped.name: Raft
dropped.reason: Donation/rounding attack exploitable against long-standing code; no recent change preceded the exploit.

dropped.name: DeltaPrime
dropped.reason: Root cause was compromise of the deployer/admin private key, not newly deployed code.

dropped.name: Wormhole
dropped.reason: Core bug was in the Solana SPL side of the bridge, not EVM code.

dropped.name: Penpie
dropped.reason: Bug was in long-standing MasterPenpie batch-registration logic; not a recent go-live.

dropped.name: Team Finance
dropped.reason: Migration (LockerTokenMigration) go-live date could not be confirmed from opened sources.

dropped.name: Hedgey Finance
dropped.reason: ClaimCampaigns contract went live Nov 22, 2023 but was exploited Apr 19, 2024 (~5 months); outside the straggler window.

dropped.name: Audius
dropped.reason: Storage-collision bug in the proxy existed since deployment; no recent upgrade preceded the exploit.
